are simulated; these exercises cannot establish a finding about a real disease.
See the [glossary](../docs/glossary.md) for the course vocabulary. Each module
loads its inputs from disk; a saved R workspace is not required.

```{r module6_setup, include=FALSE}
if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(if (file.exists("config.R")) "." else ".."))
}
source("R/guided.R")
cfg <- guided_init()
```

## 6.1 One variant by hand {#step-6-1}

### What we do

Calculate a simple carrier odds ratio at a retained autosomal site.

### Why

Odds are the number with an outcome divided by the number without it. An odds ratio (OR) compares odds between two groups; OR = 1 means equal odds. Here we compare carriers of the allele explicitly named in the exported column with non-carriers. This dominant carrier contrast is a teaching calculation, not the additive adjusted GWAS model. Allele coding matters: reversing the counted allele changes the contrast.

### You need

Full 5.7 cohort; the retained site 9:96426973:A:G.

### Command

```{r s6-1}
report <- guided_path(cfg, "6.1", "example")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), "--snp", "9:96426973:A:G", "--export", "A", "--out", report))
x <- read.table(paste0(report, ".raw"), header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE)
dose <- as.numeric(x[[7]])
psam <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), ".psam"))
case <- psam$Disease[match(x$IID, psam$IID)] == "2"
tab <- table(case = case, carrier = dose > 0)
print(tab)
carrier_or <- tab["TRUE", "TRUE"] * tab["FALSE", "FALSE"] / (tab["FALSE", "TRUE"] * tab["TRUE", "FALSE"])
print(c(counted_allele_column = names(x)[7], carrier_odds_ratio = carrier_or))
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "6.1", paste0(report, ".raw"), parent = "5.7")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s5-7_state --snp 9:96426973:A:G --export A --out results/guided/s6-1_example --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--snp` selects one variant by its exact current ID. `--export A` writes the named-allele dosage (0, 1 or 2, with missing values separate). R constructs the 2-by-2 carrier table. `--pfile` reads the final genotype state; `--out` sets the report prefix. `--threads 2` limits worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the workspace budget in MiB.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

A carrier/non-carrier table in the retained cohort and a finite odds ratio. Interpret its direction using the allele in the exported column; this need not be the allele that increases risk.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows; main test counts and significance match the instructor reference.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

An OR of 2 means that disease probability doubled. Is this statement generally correct?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. Odds and probability differ; an odds ratio is not generally a risk ratio.

</details>

### Files created

`s6-1_example.raw` and logs.

## 6.2 The additive logistic model {#step-6-2}

### What we do

Fit a one-variant logistic regression in R and connect dosage to the odds ratio.

### Why

For binary outcome Y, logistic regression models log(p/(1-p)) = intercept + beta * dosage, where p is the probability of being a case. An additive model assumes the same change in log odds for each additional counted allele. exp(beta) is the per-allele OR; it differs from the carrier contrast at 6.1. The standard error measures uncertainty in the estimated log OR. This unadjusted one-site example is not the final association result.

### You need

The one-variant export from 6.1 and the final PSAM.

### Command

```{r s6-2}
x <- read.table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "6.1", "example"), ".raw"), header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE)
psam <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), ".psam"))
example <- data.frame(case = as.numeric(psam$Disease[match(x$IID, psam$IID)] == "2"), dosage = as.numeric(x[[7]]))
fit <- glm(case ~ dosage, data = example, family = binomial())
summary(fit)
exp(coef(fit)["dosage"])
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: no PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

An intercept and dosage coefficient, with a standard error and p-value. The unadjusted per-allele OR and carrier OR need not be equal.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows; main test counts and significance match the instructor reference.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

What does beta = 0 imply for the per-allele odds ratio?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

exp(0) = 1: no estimated per-allele change in odds.

</details>

### Files created

The example model exists in R memory only; the genotype export remains on disk.

## 6.3 Prepare covariates {#step-6-3}

### What we do

Join age and ten within-cohort PCs to the retained sample IDs, and check completeness and rank.

### Why

Covariates adjust the comparison for measured predictors and structure. Misaligned covariates can invalidate every variant test while still producing plausible-looking output. Missing covariates remove observations from a model. Collinearity occurs when one column can be predicted exactly from others, preventing a unique estimate. We verify matching IDs and a full-rank design before scanning. Sex is read from PSAM and requested in the PLINK model.

### You need

State 5.7; cohort eigenvectors from 5.7; metadata from 2.7.

### Command

```{r s6-3}
psam <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), ".psam"))
pcs <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.7", "pca"), ".eigenvec"))
metadata <- guided_metadata(cfg)
a <- match(psam$IID, metadata$IID); b <- match(psam$IID, pcs$IID)
stopifnot(!anyNA(a), !anyNA(b), !anyDuplicated(pcs$IID))
covar <- data.frame(FID = psam$FID, IID = psam$IID, Age = as.numeric(metadata$Age[a]))
for (name in paste0("PC", 1:10)) covar[[name]] <- as.numeric(pcs[[name]][b])
stopifnot(!anyNA(covar))
design <- model.matrix(~ ., data = data.frame(SEX = as.numeric(psam$SEX), covar[, -(1:2)]))
stopifnot(qr(design)$rank == ncol(design))
names(covar)[1] <- "#FID"
guided_write(covar, guided_path(cfg, "6.3", "covariates.tsv"))
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "6.3", guided_path(cfg, "6.3", "covariates.tsv"), parent = "6.1")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: no PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

1,811 complete matched covariate rows with Age and PC1 to PC10. No duplicate or unmatched IDs; the design has full column rank.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows; main test counts and significance match the instructor reference.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Why is a complete covariate table with the right number of rows insufficient by itself?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

The rows must belong to the correct sample IDs and be aligned to those samples.

</details>

### Files created

`s6-3_covariates.tsv`.

## 6.4 Run the association scan {#step-6-4}

### What we do

Fit the prespecified additive logistic model with age, sex and ten PCs at every retained analysable site.

### Why

The scan tests one genetic predictor at a time while keeping the covariate specification fixed. The null hypothesis for the additive test is beta = 0. A small p-value is evidence against that null under the model and its assumptions; it does not measure effect size, causality or the probability the null is true. Firth fallback provides a more stable calculation when ordinary logistic fitting encounters separation. We do not select the covariates after inspecting the resulting peaks.

### You need

The final 5.7 genotype state and covariates from 6.3.

### Command

```{r s6-4}
out <- guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), "--maf", "0.01", "--covar", guided_path(cfg, "6.3", "covariates.tsv"),
  "--covar-name", "Age,PC1-PC10", "--covar-variance-standardize", "--glm", "sex", "hide-covar", "firth-fallback", "--out", out))
results <- guided_association(out)
valid <- valid_p(results$P)
stopifnot(sum(valid) == 236815L, sum(results$P[valid] < 5e-8) == 8L)
guided_write(results, guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "results.tsv"))
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "6.4", c(paste0(out, ".Disease.glm.logistic.hybrid"), guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "results.tsv")), parent = "6.3")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s5-7_state --maf 0.01 --covar results/guided/s6-3_covariates.tsv --covar-name Age,PC1-PC10 --covar-variance-standardize --glm sex hide-covar firth-fallback --out results/guided/s6-4_association --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--maf 0.01` rechecks the frequency rule in the final cohort. `--covar` loads the ID-keyed table. `--covar-name` selects Age and PC1 to PC10. `--covar-variance-standardize` rescales numerical covariates for stable fitting without changing the tested genetic hypothesis. `--glm sex` includes recorded sex; `hide-covar` reports genetic tests rather than every covariate coefficient; `firth-fallback` uses Firth when needed. `--pfile` reads the final genotype state; `--out` sets the report prefix. `--threads 2` limits worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the workspace budget in MiB.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

The final-cohort MAF check removes another 1,698 variants, leaving 236,815 finite additive p-values and eight below 0.00000005. A retained pre-association variant is not automatically eligible after the cohort changes. Inspect the output and log rather than replacing absent results with zero.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows; main test counts and significance match the instructor reference.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Does a tiny p-value imply a large odds ratio?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. Evidence depends on effect, uncertainty and sample size; report the effect estimate and interval too.

</details>

### Files created

`s6-4_association.Disease.glm.logistic.hybrid`, logs and a parsed `s6-4_results.tsv`.

## 6.5 Read association output {#step-6-5}

### What we do

Identify effect allele, sample count, uncertainty, test type and fitting status.

### Why

A1 is the allele whose dosage is tested, not automatically ALT, minor or harmful. OR estimates its multiplicative effect on odds. OBS_CT is the number of samples used at that variant and may vary with missing calls. ERRCODE describes model failures; a missing p-value must remain missing. A 95% confidence interval is exp(log(OR) +/- 1.96 * SE) under the fitted approximation. The interval describes estimation uncertainty under assumptions, not the chance this single interval contains a fixed truth.

### You need

The full association output from 6.4.

### Command

```{r s6-5}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
print(table(results$ERRCODE, useNA = "ifany"))
valid <- results[valid_p(results$P), ]
valid$CI_LOW <- exp(log(valid$OR) - 1.96 * valid[["LOG(OR)_SE"]])
valid$CI_HIGH <- exp(log(valid$OR) + 1.96 * valid[["LOG(OR)_SE"]])
top <- valid[order(valid$P), c("CHROM", "POS", "ID", "A1", "OBS_CT", "OR", "CI_LOW", "CI_HIGH", "P")]
print(head(top, 10))
guided_write(head(top, 20), guided_path(cfg, "6.5", "top20.tsv"))
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "6.5", guided_path(cfg, "6.5", "top20.tsv"), parent = "6.4")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: no PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

The leading regions are on chromosomes 9, 3 and 12. The table preserves the effect allele and variant-specific OBS_CT. P-values and ORs refer to the tested A1 allele, regardless of how the identifier was constructed.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows; main test counts and significance match the instructor reference.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

What should you do with a row whose ERRCODE indicates failure and whose p-value is missing?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Inspect its failure reason and retain it as missing; do not replace it with a significant or non-significant numerical value.

</details>

### Files created

`s6-5_top20.tsv` with effect estimates and intervals.

## 6.6 Sparse genotypes and Firth correction {#step-6-6}

### What we do

Compare an explicitly forced Firth fit at a low-frequency retained autosomal site.

### Why

Rare genotypes can have very few case or control observations. Ordinary logistic fitting uses maximum likelihood: it chooses coefficients that make the observed outcomes most plausible under the model. If a predictor separates outcomes completely, that coefficient can diverge. Firth penalisation reduces small-sample bias and can give finite estimates. It does not create information or fix confounding, miscalled genotypes or a poor study design. The main scan in this dataset did not actually require Firth fallback; we force it for a transparent teaching comparison at one retained low-frequency site. Sites below the 1% main-path filter are not reintroduced.

### You need

The final cohort, main results and covariates from 6.3.

### Command

```{r s6-6}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
minor <- pmin(results$A1_FREQ, 1 - results$A1_FREQ)
candidates <- which(results$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22) & valid_p(results$P) & minor > 0)
chosen <- results$ID[candidates[which.min(minor[candidates])]]
guided_list(chosen, guided_path(cfg, "6.6", "variant.txt"))
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), "--snp", chosen, "--covar", guided_path(cfg, "6.3", "covariates.tsv"),
  "--covar-name", "Age,PC1-PC10", "--covar-variance-standardize", "--glm", "firth", "sex", "hide-covar", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "6.6", "firth")))
comparison <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.6", "firth"))
print(results[results$ID == chosen, c("ID", "A1", "OR", "P")])
print(comparison[, c("ID", "A1", "OR", "P")])
stopifnot(nrow(comparison) == 1L, valid_p(comparison$P))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s5-7_state --extract results/guided/s6-6_variant.txt --covar results/guided/s6-3_covariates.tsv --covar-name Age,PC1-PC10 --covar-variance-standardize --glm firth sex hide-covar --out results/guided/s6-6_firth --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

The R command uses `--snp` with the selected ID; the equivalent terminal command uses `--extract` with its one-ID file. `--glm firth` requests Firth for that variant rather than waiting for fallback. Other covariate and resource options match 6.4. `--pfile` reads the final genotype state; `--out` sets the report prefix. `--threads 2` limits worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the workspace budget in MiB.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

One finite forced-Firth result, compared with the ordinary main-scan estimate for the same A1 allele. Small numerical differences are expected; forced Firth is not a new preferred genome-wide scan.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows; main test counts and significance match the instructor reference.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Does using Firth make an association based on very few carriers precise?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. It can stabilise fitting while uncertainty remains large.

</details>

### Files created

Selected variant ID, the forced-Firth report and logs.

## 6.7 First look and association checkpoint {#step-6-7}

### What we do

Summarise the valid tests and save the key association outputs for recovery.

### Why

A list of small p-values is not yet an interpretation. Record the model, cohort, test counts and fitting status before plotting. The next module explains multiple testing, correlated peaks and confounding comparisons. Never call a simulated lead a clinical finding or assume the nearest gene is causal.

### You need

Association output from 6.4 and reviewed table from 6.5.

### Command

```{r s6-7}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
summary <- data.frame(samples = 1811, retained_variants = 238513, finite_tests = sum(valid_p(results$P)),
  genome_wide = sum(results$P[valid_p(results$P)] < 5e-8),
  lambda_autosomes = lambda_gc(results$P[results$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)]))
guided_write(summary, guided_path(cfg, "6.7", "summary.tsv"))
print(summary)
files <- c(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"), ".Disease.glm.logistic.hybrid"),
  guided_path(cfg, "6.3", "covariates.tsv"), guided_path(cfg, "6.5", "top20.tsv"), guided_path(cfg, "6.7", "summary.tsv"))
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "6.7", files)
check_step("6.7", data_dir = cfg$out, work_dir = cfg$out)
```

## 6.8 Create the summary statistics file {#step-6-8}

### What we do

Save the results of the association scan in one clearly named file with standard columns. Write a second file that explains every column in plain words.

### Why

The raw PLINK output is long and uses PLINK column names. A summary statistics file is the standard way to share GWAS results. It holds one row per tested variant and no individual-level data. Colleagues use it to plot results, to combine studies in a meta-analysis and to look up a variant. This file keeps only the ten columns that others expect, with the same names in the same order. From now on the Manhattan and QQ plots are built from this file, not from the raw scan output.

Each column has one clear meaning. Read the table before you use the file.

| Column | What it is | What values look like | A common mistake |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chromosome` | Chromosome of the variant. | `1` to `22`, then `X`, `Y` or `MT`. | Treating it as a number. `X` is text. |
| `base_pair_location` | Position on the chromosome, in base pairs, on genome build GRCh38. | A whole number such as `96426973`. | Comparing it with positions from another genome build. |
| `variant_id` | The name of the variant in this course. | `9:96426973:A:G`: chromosome, position and the two alleles. | Expecting an rs number. This course does not use rs numbers as identifiers. |
| `effect_allele` | The allele whose copies were counted in the model. PLINK calls it A1. | One letter, such as `A`. | Assuming it is the minor allele or the ALT allele. It is neither by definition. |
| `other_allele` | The other allele of the variant. | One letter, such as `G`. | Swapping the two alleles. The odds ratio then points the other way. |
| `effect_allele_frequency` | How common the effect allele is in the analysed samples. | A number from 0 to 1, such as `0.2`. | Reading it as the minor allele frequency. It can be above 0.5. |
| `odds_ratio` | The odds ratio per copy of the effect allele. | A positive number. Above 1 means higher odds of disease with each copy. | Reading it as a risk ratio. |
| `standard_error` | The standard error of the natural logarithm of the odds ratio. | A small positive number, such as `0.09`. | Using it as the standard error of the odds ratio itself. It belongs to the log odds ratio. |
| `p_value` | The p-value of the additive test. | A number above 0 and at most 1. A test that failed is `NA`. | Replacing `NA` with 1 or 0. A missing result stays missing. |
| `n` | The number of samples used for this variant. | A whole number up to 1,811. | Assuming every variant uses all samples. Missing genotypes lower it. |

To get the 95% confidence interval of an odds ratio, use `exp(log(odds_ratio) +/- 1.96 * standard_error)`. This is why the standard error is on the log scale.

The file is tab-separated text with a header row, UTF-8 encoding and decimal points. It holds only results per variant. It has no genotypes and no sample IDs. Even so, keep it out of the repository, like every other result file.

### You need

The association scan from 6.4 and the summary from 6.7.

### Command

```{r s6-8}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
stats <- guided_standardise_scan(results)
guided_check_summary(stats, rows = nrow(results))
stats_file <- guided_summary_path(cfg)
guided_write_summary(stats, stats_file)
dictionary_file <- guided_path(cfg, "6.8", "gwas_summary_statistics_columns.tsv")
guided_write(guided_summary_dictionary(), dictionary_file)
# Read the file back, as the plots will, and check that nothing was lost.
saved <- guided_summary_stats(cfg)
guided_check_summary(saved, rows = nrow(results))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(saved, stats)))
first_summary <- read.delim(guided_path(cfg, "6.7", "summary.tsv"))
finite <- valid_p(saved$p_value)
stopifnot(sum(finite) == first_summary$finite_tests, sum(saved$p_value[finite] < 5e-8) == first_summary$genome_wide)
print(head(saved, 5))
print(c(rows = nrow(saved), finite_tests = sum(finite), missing_p_values = sum(is.na(saved$p_value)),
  genome_wide = sum(saved$p_value[finite] < 5e-8)))
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "6.8", c(stats_file, dictionary_file), parent = "6.7")
check_step("6.8", data_dir = cfg$out, work_dir = cfg$out)
```

### Quick check

Your colleague wants the 95% confidence interval for an odds ratio. Which column do they use together with `odds_ratio`, and on which scale?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

They use `standard_error`. It is the standard error of the natural logarithm of the odds ratio. The interval is calculated on the log scale and then converted back with `exp()`.
